summary: Coos County, NH summit lookout set up by the NH Timberland Owners in 1910 (1911 in one report); cabin closed 1980, burned 1982; ledges and small relics remain.

facts.design: Cabin on the bare rock summit, described as a fire tower in some sources; last cabin built in the mid-1960s
facts.status_note: The last cabin was closed in 1980 and burned in 1982; blots in the ledges, a USGS benchmark and part of an old cast iron stove remain

access.note: On Nash Stream State Forest land; reached by an old road of about 2.1 miles that a hike report describes as steep, reached via Emerson Road and the gravel Nash Stream Road

visit.trail_note: Hike the old road to the former fire tower site; no tower or cabin stands, only ledges and remnants

facts.agency: NH Timberland Owners Association built the lookout; the site was on Groveton Paper Co. land

events.note: A lookout station was established at this point in 1910, per the Forest Lookouts page citing a Report of the Forestry Commissioner; the NH Timberland Owners Association paid for seven 1910 lookouts including Sugarloaf
A hike report gives 1911 for a cabin established on the summit by the NH Timberland Owners on Groveton Paper Co. land
The last cabin, built in the mid-1960s, was closed in 1980
The last cabin burned in 1982; a listing site describes remnants of the burned lookout near the upper trail

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts, NH Family Hikes and White Mountain History tie the Timberland Owners' summit lookout to 1910; the Weirs.com hike report gives 1911. The story uses 1910 and mentions the 1911 report.

The Weirs.com report describes a cabin on the bare rock summit, the listing site calls it a fire lookout tower, and the lookout list records the kind as ground. The facts record calls it a cabin described as a tower in some sources.

sources.title: Nash Stream State Forest - Sugarloaf and South Percy

notes_for_editor: Two hike reports (Weirs.com, List Hiker) carry most of the post-1960 history and the site description; neither is an official record. The 1910 and 1911 dates conflict. The 1910 date comes from a forestry commissioner report quoted by Forest Lookouts and from general NHTOA history. No staffing names appear in any source read. A geocaching page gives a 1919 build date and 1980 closure, but the page text could not be read, so it is not used. Oregon's Sugarloaf Mountain Forest Lookouts pages (oregonlookouts.weebly.com) are a different site and were excluded. Elevation is 3,701 ft in one source and 3,703 ft in another; the story gives neither. No photos added.
